rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAM, INCREASING COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS FOR BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS (BHW), APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to apply the provisions of this Act to all BHWs under Republic Act. No.7883; Defines “barangay health worker” as person who has undergone a training program under any accredited government or non-government organization.
Includes provisions regarding accreditation and competency assessment; program cost and cost sharing for LGUS; Compensations based on PhilHealth utilization, mandatory continuing community-based health education; compensation and other incentives (monthly basic pay of P6,000.00; benefits under the Magna Carta for Public Health Workers; PAG-IBIG/GSIS/PhilHealth; burial and disability assistance).
rows.status: Substituted by HB06557

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE SALE OF CASKETS BY FUNERAL ESTABLISHMENTS TO ENSURE AVAILABILITY OF AFFORDABLE CASKETS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Proposes that all funeral establishments shall at all times maintain available decent caskets with a price of not more than Twenty Thousand Pesos (P20,000.00). In case of unavailability, the establishment shall be obliged to offer one of any higher value but the indigent family or extremely poor family shall still pay an amount of not more than P20,000.00.
rows.status: Transmitted to the President on 2025-08-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PROTECTING ELDERLY FROM ABUSE, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFORE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to provide senior citizens who are victims of violence, with protection and the necessary assistance to ensure their personal safety and security.
Defines “violence against the elderly” to any type of violence or abuse, whether physical abuse or violence, sexual, psychological or emotional abuse, material or financial exploitation, and neglect, inflicted upon an elderly individual.

rows.author: G059;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING BUDGET REFORM THAT WILL ENSURE THE EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION OF FUNDS FOR BOTH THE NATIONAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROMOTING VILLAGE EMPOWERMENT, ENABLING THEM TO BE AN EFFECTIVE INSTRUMENT IN ATTAINING INCLUSIVE GROWTH, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to institutionalize a rational and equitable budget distribution for LGU development with a more systematic, targeted and rigorous balance of the budget from national agencies to local governments.
Proposes that the “Local Development Fund” (LDF) shall be divided among the different political subdivisions solely for developmental projects, activities and programs (PAPs) based on the approved Comprehensive Development Plans (CDPs).
Seeks to appropriate adequate funds for “Local Government Academy” (LGA) to provide LGUs with the necessary tools in undertaking effective planning and proper implementation of their PAPs in accordance with their CDPs.
rows.status: Referred to Stakeholders on 2022-11-07

rows.author: G059;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR PARENT SUPPORT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to further strengthen filial responsibility and make it a criminal offense in case of flagrant violation thereof, as in abandonment of a parent in need of support. Such parent may file a petition for support before the court and pray for the issuance of a support order against their erring children.
Proposes to establish Old Age Home for the elderly, sick or otherwise incapacitated parents in every province and highly urbanized cities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR FALSIFICATION                   OF CERTIFICATES OF LAND TITLE OR ANY APPLICATION, DEED, INSTRUMENT OR SUPPORTING DOCUMENT, REASONABLY CONNECTED WITH AND CALCULATED TO CAUSE THE ISSUANCE OF A CERTIFICATE OF LAND TITLE, CLASSIFYING THE SAME AS HEINOUS OFFENSE INVOLVING ECONOMIC SABOTAGE IF THE VALUE OR AGGREGATE VALUE OF THE LAND IS AT LEAST TEN MILLION PESOS (P10,000,000.00), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 171 AND 172 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS, THE REVISED PENALCODE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
rows.abstract:
Seeks to remedy and stop the nefarious practice of anomalously titling of land by increasing its penalty. . .
Seeks to refer Certificate of Land Title to evidence of ownership issued pursuant to the order of the court over registered land or the muniment of title issued by a government administrative agency for the conveyance of some portion of public domain. It includes, but it is not limited to the Original Certificates of Title (OCT), Transfer Certificates of Title (TCT), Certificate of Land Ownership Awards (CLOA), Land Patents, Sales Patents, Homestead Patents, and Free Patents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2022-07-26

rows.abstract:
Proposes among other various provisions that the Department shall exercise administrative supervision over several agencies for policy and program coordination, monitoring, and evaluation: Local Water Utilities Administration (LWUA); Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS); National Irrigation Administration (NIA).
Proposes further that several offices (their functions, and personnel) shall be completely subsumed under the Department, as follows:  National Water Resources Board; River Basin Control Office; Manila Bay Coordinating Office; Water Resources Management Division of the Bureau of Soils and Water Management of the Department of Agriculture; Water Supply and Sanitation Unit of the DILG; and the Water Quality Management Section of the Environmental Management Bureau of the DENR.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENTAL AUTHORITY TO INSTITUTIONALIZE A TECHNICAL-VOCATIONAL EDUCATION AND TRAINING AND LIVELIHOOD PROGRAM DESIGNED SPECIFICALLY FOR REHABILITATED DRUG DEPENDENTS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Proposes to institutionalize trainings and programs through the TESDA for the benefit of drug dependents undergoing rehabilitation treatment.
rows.status: Substituted by HB07721

rows.author: J014;J057;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2023-08-16, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-08-22 and received by the Senate on 2023-08-22
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING STRONGER MEASURES FOR THE CONSERVATION AND PROTECTION OF WILDLIFE RESOURCES AND THEIR HABITATS, REPEALING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9147, OR THE "WILDLIFE RESOURCES CONSERVATION AND PROTECTION ACT", AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Proposes among others, the following provisions:
The DENR shall have jurisdiction over all terrestrial plant and animal species including turtles and tortoises, wetland species, including crocodiles, waterbirds and all amphibians and the Dugong, Dugon or Dugong; the Department of Agriculture shall have jurisdiction over all declared aquatic critical habitats, all aquatic resources including all fishes, aquatic plants, invertebrates and all marine mammals, except Dugong; in the Province of Palawan, jurisdiction is vested on the Palawan Council for Strategic Development (PCSD) pursuant to R.A. No.7611 or the Strategic Environment Plan (SEP) for Palawan Act.
Defines several terms among others such as biodiversity, critically endangered species, indigenous wildlife; invasive alien species, and critical habitat (an area outside protected areas under R.A. No.7586 or the National Integrated Protected Area System (NIPAS) Act, as amended by R.A. No.11038 or the ENIPAS, that are known habitats of threatened species and designated based on scientific data taking into consideration species endemicity and richness, and the presence of manmade pressures and threats to the survival of wildlife living in the area, among others.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08586

rows.author: J014;J057;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2023-05-08, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-05-09 and received by the Senate on 2023-05-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR MANDATORY INSURANCE COVERAGE AND BENEFITS FOR ALL LINE WORKERS
rows.abstract:
Seeks to mandate that all line workers shall be entitled to life and accident or disability insurance benefits in accordance with the classification standards which provides for a minimum required coverage of P200,000.00 for small distribution utilities up to P1,000.000.00 for mega large distribution utilities, and P2,000,000.00 for transmission or grid operator.
Provides that employers of line workers shall also grant additional mandatory benefits: Retirement benefits, Mortuary assistance, Disability benefits, and reimbursement of actual medical expenses in case of death, accident sickness, disability or injury sustained by the line workers in the line of duty.
rows.status: Substituted by HB07561

rows.author: J014;J057;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FREE ANNUAL MEDICAL CHECK-UP FOR FILIPINOS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFORE
rows.abstract: Seeks to entitle all Filipino citizens (by virtue of their membership in PhilHealth mandated under “Universal Health Care Law”), to a free medical check-up in any government hospital, that shall include blood sugar and cholesterol tests.  Laboratory and diagnostic tests shall be expanded, subject to the availability of PhilHealth funds.
rows.status: Measure approved by the Committee on 2023-02-15

committee_action.action: Measure approved by the Committee on 2023-02-15

rows.author: J014;J057;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2023-05-29, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-05-30 and received by the Senate on 2023-05-30
rows.title_full: AN ACT REVERTING FISHPONDS WHICH HAVE BEEN UNUTILIZED OR ABANDONED FOR A PERIOD OF THREE (5) YEARS TO FOREST LANDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 43 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO.705 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “THE REVISED FORESTRY REFORM CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES”
rows.abstract:
Seeks to shorten the period to revert fishponds to forest lands from five (5) years to THREE (3) YEARS only.
Proposes that the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources shall jointly set guidelines for determining abandoned, undeveloped or underutilized fishponds . . . which shall be reverted into forestlands and to be rehabilitated.
rows.status: Substituted by HB07754

rows.author: K053;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF DISASTER RESILIENCE, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Proposes to create a separate Department of Disaster Resilience aimed at reducing the risk of all types of natural hazards and the harmful effects of climate change.
Seeks to identify three (3) key result areas to be focused upon by the Department:  Disaster Risk Reduction; Disaster Preparedness and Response; and Recovery and Building Forward Better.
Proposes among others:  the establishment of an Integrated Disaster Resilience Information System (IDRIS); the creation of an early warning system which shall make use of risk communication protocols; and the establishment of a Humanitarian Assistance Action Center (HAAC).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2022-07-26

rows.author: K053;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2022-12-12, transmitted to the Senate on 2022-12-14 and received by the Senate on 2022-12-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms among others such as “Disease Surveillance”; “Epidemic/Outbreak; “Public Health Emergency”.
Proposes that the Center shall be responsible for the tracking and monitoring diseases and risk factors among Filipinos -  to inform policy and action at national and local levels; and shall be the focal point for the implementation at the local level of international health regulations and other international initiatives for global health security and outbreak response.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06522

committee_action.action: Committee Report filed on 2022-12-06

rows.author: E046;K107;
rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE CAP OF PHASING OUT SYSTEM LOSSES TO CONSUMERS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 10 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7832
rows.abstract:
Intends to address the fact that the Philippines ranks as having the highest electrical rate per kilowatt-hour in the whole ASEAN region, more particularly residential users.
Seeks to entirely prohibit distribution utilities from passing on non-technical system losses to consumers and to mitigate the impact of technical system losses to the minimum - Components of System Losses include technical losses (losses inherent in the physical delivery of electrical energy) and non-technical losses (not related to the physical characteristics and functions of the electrical system, and are caused primarily by human error, whether intentional or not - like pilferage).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: E046;K107;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING EXEMPTION FROM IMPOSITION OF VALUE-ADDED TAXES (VAT) ON THE ELECTRICAL BILLINGS OF RESIDENTIAL HOUSEHOLDS WITH A TOTAL MONTHLY CONSUMPTION OF 200KWH AND LESS
rows.abstract:
Aims to mitigate the burden to consumers of costly electricity, especially those living below the poverty line, the poor and marginalized sector of the community.
Intends to address the fact that “an electricity bill is riddled with various components with additional VAT imposition - . . .Except for universal, and feed-in-tariff allowance charges, the rest of the components include the imposition of VAT.  Under the TRAIN Law . . ., a twelve percent (12% VAT) is imposed on the sale of electricity, transmission by any entity, including the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines, and distribution companies, including electric cooperatives.
rows.status: Referred to Stakeholders on 2022-08-02

committee_action.action: Referred to Stakeholders on 2022-08-02

rows.author: E046;K107;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING THE RENEWABLE ENERGY INDUSTRY THROUGH THE GREEN ENERGY AUCTION PROGRAM
rows.abstract:
Defines Green Energy Auction Reserve Price or GEAR Price - to the maximum price offers in PhP/kWh set by the ERC pursuant to applicable laws . . . factoring other RE technologies, such as Floating Solar Projects and Offshore Wind Projects.
Seeks to establish the Green Energy Auction to provide for the framework of the GEAP and a mechanism to facilitate the selection of eligible RE plants through competitive selection process.
Tasks the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) to determine the Green Energy Auction Reserve Price (“Gear Price”) which will be the Feed-in-Tariff (FIT) ceiling for each round of the GEAP, where qualified participants may offer capacity generation for a rate not higher than the GEAR Price.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: E046;K107;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A RENEWABLE ENERGY (RE) PARK OVER LAGUNA BAY TO ACCELERATE THE RENEWABLE ENERGY CAPACITY IN THE PHILIPPINES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THIS PURPOSE
rows.abstract: Seeks to establish an initial exclusive zone for renewable energy park with promising potential for large-scale floating solar power farms and projects; Tasks the DOE to determine the maximum energy capacity of the Renewable Energy Park which may be used for the development and operation of other renewable energy projects such as hydropower facilities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: E046;K107;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROTECT THE FILIPINO CONSUMERS FROM ARBITRARY INCREASES IN THE PRICES OF LPG BEING CHARGED BY THE PLAYERS OF THE LPG INDUSTRY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 19 AND 14 OF R.A. 8479, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS DOWNSTREAM OIL INDUSTRY DEREGULATION LAW OF 1998
rows.abstract: Provides that the price of LPG has to be guided by an Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) which shall be determined by the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC); Seeks to ensure that only safe and qualified LPG cylinders are put in circulation by providing for cylinder repair and maintenance cost.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: E046;K107;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE MANDATORY ENVIRONMENTAL INSURANCE COVERAGE OF ENVIRONMENTALLY CRITICAL PROJECTS
rows.abstract:
Seeks to require Mandatory Environmental Insurance Coverage for owners and operators of environmentally-critical projects whose activities destroy or pose risks to the environment, the ecosystems and their constituent elements; Provides that said insurance shall guarantee sufficient funding coverage for the needed restoration and compensate for damages caused by their operations.
Provides that Environmentally-Critical Projects (ECPs) shall include heavy industries, major manufacturing industries, major resource-extractive industries, major infrastructure projects, and other similar projects that could pose serious risks to people and the environment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: E046;K107;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2023-12-12, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-12-13 and received by the Senate on 2023-12-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A PRESCRIPTIVE PERIOD FROM WHICH COA MAY CONDUCT AUDITS AND ISSUE A DECISION ON CASES, AMENDING THE STATE AUDIT CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES (P.D. 1445) FOR SUCH PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to address COA´s practice of conducting post-audit many years after the grant of the fund to the implementing agencies (IAs) and NGO/PO partners which does not sit well with its time-bound monitoring and inspection audit function.
Proposes that a prescriptive period of two (2) years shall be strictly observed to reflect the preventive nature of the Commission´s function in relation to its visitorial authority to non-government entities subsidized by the government . . . pertaining only to the authority of those funds or subsidies coming from or through the government, and  over non-governmental entities whose loans are guaranteed by the Government, . . . provided that such authority shall pertain only to the audit of the government´s contingent liability.
Proposes further that in the discharge of powers, functions, and duties of auditors as representatives of the Commission, “a prescriptive audit period of two (2) years shall be strictly observed from the completion of a project which financial transaction or undertaking is the subject matter of such audit.”
rows.status: Substituted by HB09674

rows.author: E046;K107;
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO INTRODUCE STRUCTURAL AND INSTITUTIONAL ADJUSTMENTS INTO THE K TO 12 CURRICULUM TO ACHIEVE GREATER EFFICIENCY AND SUCCESS ACROSS ALL KEY STAGES OF THE PROGRAM
rows.abstract:
Introduces a broad range of provisions which are categorized as follows:  a) teacher qualifications; b) class size/hours; c) curricular content review; d) instruction (including learning resources); e) convergence/synergy; f) general provisions.
Proposes several detailed provisions among others as follows:  master´s degree for teachers and intensified Science and Math instruction training; reduce class sizes, class hours, and time spent on schoolwork; English and Filipino as medium of instruction from Grade 4 onwards, standardized tests at the end of students´ 6th grade and senior year in high school as basis for promotion; only 5 subjects such as Math, Science, Language, Practical Life, and Sensory or Psychomotor activities to primary or elementary level; a Science H.S.  to include agriculture and disaster preparedness; and Entrepreneurship subject to junior and senior high school.
Proposes further that all companies shall be required to institute a Work Immersion Program to absorb senior high school students as internship or as OJT; removal of ranking and class standing or any parameter that promotes competition or comparison; conversion of homework to classwork; and self-paced weekly targets with teachers and the freedom to choose the tasks they will work on.
rows.alias_name: “Building Blocks to the Enhanced K to 12 Program Act”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2022-07-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PANIQUI TARLAC ECO-FARM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Substituted by HB07324

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2023-11-07, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-11-09 and received by the Senate on 2023-11-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PANIQUI TARLAC TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (TESDA) TRAINING CENTER AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Substituted by HB09017

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NET METERING SYSTEM AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9513 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE RENEWABLE ENERGY (RE) LAW OF 2008
rows.abstract:
Proposes amendments to “distributed generation” which is a system of small generation entities supplying directly to the distribution grid, with enumerated capacity for specified period.
Tasks the Department of Energy (DOE) as the lead agency together with the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC), and other public and private stakeholders representing consumers and sectors affected by this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE SURVEY, UTILIZATION, AND DEVELOPMENT OF IDLE AND UNUTILIZED ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES (AFP) REAL ESTATES FOR POTENTIAL SITES OF RENEWABLE ENERGY PROJECTS
rows.abstract: Aims to promote the exploration and development of Renewable Energy (RE) resources to reduce the country´s dependence and reliance on imported fossil fuels and thereby minimize exposure to price fluctuations in the international markets.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ENERGY INVESTMENT COORDINATING COUNCIL (EICC), STRENGTHENING AND FURTHER DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Seeks to strengthen the role of the Energy Investment Coordinating Council (EICC) to further ease and integrate government processes to attract/harness more energy investments in the country, particularly for Energy Projects of National Significance (EPNS), considering the threat of an energy crisis on a global scale, as well as the thinning energy resources on the national scale.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.mother_status: Republic Act RA12120 enacted on 2025-01-08
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEVELOPING THE PHILIPPINES´ NATURAL GAS INDUSTRY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THIS PURPOSE
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms among others including Downstream Natural Gas Industry which refers to the business of importing exporting, re-exporting, shipping, transporting, processing, refining, storing, distributing, marketing, and/or selling natural gas.
Takes into account the nearing expiration of the Malampaya concessions by 2024 wherein we still do not have any alternative either in imported or indigenous sources; that the supply can go as far as 2027 but it does not have enough gas to further expansion to provide the future natural gas requirements, particularly on the plan to expand the application of natural gas in industrial, commercial, residential, and transport sectors.
rows.alias_name: “Development of the Downstream Natural Gas Act”
rows.status: Substituted by HB08456

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING CROSS-OWNERSHIP AS AMONG DISTRIBUTION UTILITIES AND GENERATION COMPANIES AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 45 OF REPUBLIC ACT (RA) NO. 9136
rows.abstract:
Proposes the following amendments to be read as follows:
	“SEC. 45. Cross Ownership, Market Power Abuse and Anti-competitive Behavior - ”¦
	“To promote true market competition and prevent harmful monopoly and market power abuse, the ERC shall enforce the following safeguards:
(a)	. . .
(b)	. . . For the purpose of preventing market power abuse between associated firms engaged in generation and distribution, BY NO MEANS CAN DISTRIBUTION UTILITIES ENTER INTO BILATERAL POWER SUPPLY AGREEMENTS WITH ANY ASSOCIATED FIRM ENGAGED IN GENERATION, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT.  THIS SHALL NOT PREJUDICE CONTRACTCTS ENTERED INTO PRIOR TO THE EFFECTTIVIY OF THIS ACT    . . .THE IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS OF THE ACT IS TO BE ADJUSTED ACCORDINGLY WITHOUT REDEFINING “CONTROL” AS DEFINED IN THIS SECTION . . .
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXCLUDING THE SERVICES PERFORMED BY EMPLOYEES OF RELIGIOUS ENTITIES FROM EMPLOYMENT SERVICES COVERED BY SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM LAW, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO.8282 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "SOCIAL SECURITY ACT OF 1997"
rows.abstract: Seeks to exlude from the coverage of R.A. No.8282, the “service performed in the employ of a foundation, association or corporation, organized and operated exclusively for religious purposes:  Provided, that the employees . . . voluntarily perform their duties fully directly, and solely for religious activities . . .:  Provided further, that said employees are active and devoted members of these religious entities:  Provided, finally, that these entities provide said  employees with decent housing and basic medical services, aside from the modest financial allowances they receive to support themselves and/or their families: . . .
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2022-07-26

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS SOCIAL SECURITY AND RETIREMENT SYSTEM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Aims to allow OFWs to receive retirement pay at an earlier age or to receive voluntary separation benefits upon their retirement.
Seeks to establish a retirement system designed to provide the OFWs with funds they can use to engage in other productive endeavors when they decide to finally retire or separate from work.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2022-07-26

rows.author: 0000;K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE IMPOSITION OF FEES FOR THE USE OF PARKING SPACES AND/OR FACILITIES PROVIDED BY   OR LOCATED WITHIN SHOPPING MALLS, SCHOOLS, HOSPITALS, HOTELS AND SIMILAR ESTABLISHMENTS AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREOF FOR VIOLATIONS
rows.abstract: Proposes to prohibit the collection of parking fees within the first three (3) hours from the time of the customer´s entry to the parking premises of several establishments, and to Impose a regular fee if he exceeds the allowed free parking hours, provided that if the said customer purchase a product/s or service/s whose value  is not less than P1,000.00, he can avail a discount rebate of 10% of the assessed regular parking fee.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE DECLARATION OF THE VALUE IMPORTED GOODS IN SHIPPING AND AIRLINE DOCUMENTS AND PROHIBITING FRAUDULENT ALTERATION OF CARGO MANIFEST, BILL OF LADING, AND AIRWAY BILL AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10863, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "CUSTOMS MODERNIZATION AND TARIFF ACT"
rows.abstract:
Aims to significantly deter the use of commercial and shipping documents in smuggling and illegal importation activities.
Seeks to ensure consistency of commercial documents transmitted and presented to Philippine authorities - the Pier Inspection Division or the Aircraft Operations Division and the District Collector of the Port, as the case may who are tasked to reconcile the hard copy of the cargo manifest with the electronic cargo manifest of a vessel from a foreign port.
rows.status: Deliberated upon by the Mother Committee on 2022-11-28

committee_action.action: Deliberated upon by the Mother Committee on 2022-11-28

rows.author: K107;E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE IMPOUNDING OF MOTOR VEHICLES INVOLVED IN A VEHICULAR INCIDENT THAT RESULTED IN THE DEATH OR SERIOUS PHYSICAL INJURY OF A PEDESTRIAN, COMMUTER OR BY-STANDER, UNLESS A CASH BOND IS POSTED
rows.abstract: Seeks to make it mandatory for the court to be held in custodia legis, the vehicle involved in an accident or require the owner or operator to post a cash bond of at least Php500,000.00 - pending the outcome of any criminal or civil proceeding as security for the satisfaction of any judgment that may be rendered.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2022-07-26

rows.author: I034;
rows.mother_status: Passed by the Senate with amendments on 2024-09-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING JUNE 15 OF EVERY YEAR A SPECIAL NONWORKING HOLIDAY IN THE PROVINCE OF PAMPANGA TO BE KNOWN AS THE "MT. PINATUBO MEMORIAL DAY"
rows.status: Substituted by HB04838

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING MT. ARAYAT, BORDERING THE MUNICIPALITIES OF ARAYAT AND MAGALANG, PROVINCE OF PAMPANGA AS A TOURIST DESTINATION, PROVIDING FOR ITS DEVELOPMENT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Substituted by HB05169

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A BARANGAY TO BE KNOWN AS BARANGAY PULUNG BULU IN THE CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, PROVINCE OF PAMPANGA
rows.status: Substituted by HB06013

rows.author: I034;
rows.mother_status: Transmitted to the President on 2025-08-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING, AMONG OTHERS, SECTIONS 4, 5, AND 6 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10752 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS "THE RIGHT-OF-WAY ACT
rows.status: Substituted by HB06571

rows.author: I034;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE CONSOLIDATION OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS, TITLING OF UNTITLED AGRICULTURAL LANDS, PROVIDING FOR POST-HARVEST FACILITIES TO RICE FARMERS, ESTABLISHING IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM TO LAND OWNER/FARMER AND AGRICULTURAL TENANTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Tasks the DENR-Land Management Bureau to undertake a ten (10)-year program for the purpose of mapping, surveying, consolidating, and titling of all untitled agricultural land on a per province undertaking.
Proposes to establish a state-of-the-art rice milling facilities and palay drying equipment in every province and provides state-of-the-art agricultural equipment and machinery to aid local farmers in producing a high variety of rice.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AD HOC COMMITTEE ON AGRICULTURE SERVICES CONVERGENCE INITIATIVE since 2024-07-29

rows.author: I034;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2024-11-19, transmitted to the Senate on 2024-11-21 and received by the Senate on 2024-11-21
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR PROTECTION OF THE REMITTANCES OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS
rows.abstract:
Intends to protect the hard-earned money of OFWs against exorbitant fees charged by financial institutions that deplete the value of their remittances; and to provide them and their families with adequate education and training on financial literacy, such as financial planning and management of finances or savings.
Proposes several provisions among others as follows:  discount on remittance fees and tax deduction granted to establishments based on the cost of services to OFWs; requirement of posting of the peso equivalent of the currency to be exchanged; prohibition from raising remittance fees, including other prohibited acts.
rows.status: Substituted by HB10959

committee_action.action: Measure approved by the Committee on 2022-10-13

rows.author: I034;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF CIVIL ENGINEERING AND REPEALING FOR THAT PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 544, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1582
rows.abstract: Aims to continually upgrade the level of competence of civil engineers through peer recognition of specialization; continuing professional development including research; and strengthening the accredited professional organization through 1) ensuring the capabilities of our aspiring civil engineers and monitoring the practice of present civil engineers; 2) widening the scope of licensure examinations to include a vital subject in the National Building Code; 3) allowing specialization in different areas in the practice of CE (CE Education; Construction Management and Engineering; Energy and Environmental Systems Engineering; Geotechnical Engineering; Hydraulic and Water Resources Engineering; Structural Engineering; Transportation Engineering, etc.)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2022-07-26

rows.author: I034;
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4566, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "CONTRACTORS' LICENSE LAW", AS AMENDED, PROVIDING FOR THE TYPES, ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS, AND REQUIREMENTS IN THE ISSUANCE OF A CONTRACTORS´ LICENSE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Seeks to prioritize Filipino contractors and workers in the construction industry which will enable them to engage in the business for multiple projects as long as such license remains valid.  Provides that the foreign contractors may also engage in the construction business, but under a special license, and for a single specified undertaking only; that a regular license may still be issued under specific instances; that foreign contractors shall not be considered for the grant of license unless their country of States of Origin allows Filipino contractors to practice within their territory on the same bases as its subjects or citizens.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2022-07-26

rows.author: E003;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION ON THE BASIS OF ETHNICITY, RACE, RELIGION OR BELIEF, SEX OR GENDER OR SEXUAL ORIENTATION, LANGUAGE, DISABILITY, EDUCATIONAL ATTAINMENT, AND OTHER FORMS OF DISCRIMINATION, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to prevent and criminalize various forms of discrimination that may be categorized as a crime against humanity and human dignity, based on several international declarations that promote the equal treatment of all people.
Provides for corresponding penalties to such discriminatory acts as inflicting stigma, denial of education, political, civil, and cultural rights, right to work, access to goods and services, and the right to organize, inflicting harm on health and well-being, engaging in profiling, abuses by state and non-state agencies, and detention and confinement.
Defines several terms:  discrimination, profiling, stigma, vulnerable communities, and indigenous peoples, among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2022-07-26

rows.author: E003;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING SOCIAL SECURITY AND ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO ALL BARANGAY OFFICIALS, WORKERS, AND VOLUNTEERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND  FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Seeks to provide to all barangay workers and volunteers - social security benefits under the program of the GSIS, PhilHealth, and Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2022-07-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE SOCIAL PENSION OF INDIGENT SENIOR CITIZENS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432 ENTITLED, "AN ACT TO MAXIMIZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION BUILDING, GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES", AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Refers the term SOCIAL PENSION to the monetary grant from the government to support the daily subsistence and medical needs of senior citizens which SHALL NOT BE LESS THAN ONE THOUSAND PESOS (P1,000.00) PER MONTH.
Seeks to make mandatory the entitlement of social pension to indigent senior citizens.
rows.status: Tabled by the Committee on 2022-11-08

rows.author: C100;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2022-12-12, transmitted to the Senate on 2022-12-14 and received by the Senate on 2022-12-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE USE OF TREATMENT TECHNOLOGY FOR MUNICIPAL AND HAZARDOUS WASTES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 20 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8749, ENTITLED "THE PHILIPPINE CLEAN AIR ACT OF 1999"
rows.abstract:
Seeks to amend “The Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999” and “The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000” pertaining to the ban on the incineration of waste to reduce and resolve the garbage issue of every LGUs and minimize further damage to our environment and ecological system.
Proposes to set the standards on the use of treatment technologies for the disposal of municipal and hazardous wastes, or for the processing of any waste material for fuel; Mandates the DENR to implement and enforce this Act, including the promotion and use of modern technology, environment-friendly and safe technologies for the treatment, utilization, and disposal of residual wastes.
Provides for the roles of the DOST and the DOE; the responsibilities of owners and operators; the grant of incentives to investors and hosts of waste treatment programs.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06444

rows.author: C100;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2023-05-29, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-05-30 and received by the Senate on 2023-05-30
rows.title_full: AN ACT MODERNIZING THE BUREAU OF IMMIGRATION BY DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, FURTHER PROFESSIONALIZING ITS ORGANIZATION, UPGRADING THE COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS OF ITS OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to strengthen the organizational structure of the Bureau with expanded jurisdiction and streamlined powers and functions; to comply with the obligations and standards set by international law in the admission or exclusion of foreign nationals; to promote int´l order and justice by denying the use of Phil. Territory to persons who are engaged or likely to engage in terrorism, human smuggling and trafficking, criminal and other nefarious activities.
Provides for an Immigration Trust Fund (ITF) for the modernization of equipment, facilities and offices, including capital outlay for new buildings and field offices; payment of employee benefits; and further professionalization of the employees.  
Intends to harmonize existing immigration rules and regulations pertaining to issuance of visas to foreign nationals.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08203

rows.author: C100;
rows.mother_status: Republic Act RA11983 enacted on 2024-03-11
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NEW PASSPORT LAW, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8239, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "PHILIPPINE PASSPORT ACT OF1996"
rows.abstract:
Seeks to mandate the issuance of passports using tamper proof and the latest data management technology; Simplifies the documentation requirements of the DFA - Office of the Consular Affairs, in conformity with existing laws and standards set by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO); Implement a system wherein senior citizens may renew their passports without a personal appearance.
Proposes to require the DFA to create different databases containing all current and previous passport and travel document records; a watch list containing the name of persons whose applications have been denied or revoked; names and information of persons who committed passport-related offenses.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06510

rows.author: C100;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF DISASTER RESILIENCE, DEFINING ITS MANDATE, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to create a new Department which shall be the sole policy-making and advisory body on disaster risk and vulnerability reduction and management and build better forward as a post-recovery and post-rehabilitation mechanism.
Proposes among others the abolition of the existing National Disaster Risk Reduction Management Council, while the assets and personnel of the Office of Civil Defense under the DND shall be transferred to the proposed Department.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2022-07-26

rows.author: C100;
rows.mother_status: Republic Act RA12001 enacted on 2024-06-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING REFORMS IN REAL PROPERTY VALUATION AND ASSESSMENT IN THE PHILIPPINES, REORGANIZING THE BUREAU OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Aims to address the following systemic problems in real property valuation and assessment:  rampant outdated valuations; cost overruns and foregone revenues due to low valuations used; multiple, overlapping valuations - no single agency responsible for ensuring that valuations are completed in accordance with international standards; and absence of a comprehensive real property electronic database.
Seeks to adopt a market-based Schedule of Market Values (SMV) to be used as a basis for local and national real property taxation which will widen the tax base used for property and property-related taxes.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06558

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REVISED WAREHOUSE RECEIPTS LAW OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Providing For The Revised Warehouse Receipts Law Of The Philippines
rows.abstract:
Aims to establish a simplified, unified, and modern framework for the storage of goods in warehouses and the subsequent trading of interest therein.

Proposes to establish a central electronic Registry for all warehouse receipts which will be made readily available online and eventually integrated with other existing Registries.

Enables the agricultural sector to convert goods and products into credit in a faster and simpler way, promote economic activity by increasing access, particularly for entities engaged in agricultural businesses such as farming, to least cost credit.

Provides for the following provisions: 1.) Obligations and rights of warehouse operators upon their receipts; 2.) Negotiation and transfer of receipt; and 3.) Criminal Offenses, among others.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-05-29, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-05-30 and received by the Senate on 2023-05-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT REPEALING THE RESERVA TRONCAL PROVISION PROVIDED FOR UNDER ARTICLE 891 OF THE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 386, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NEW CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Repeals Art. 891 of the Civil Code which states that:
The ascendant who inherits from his descendant any property which the latter may have acquired by gratuitous title from another ascendant, or a brother or sister, is obliged to reserve such property as he may have acquired by operation of law for the benefit of relatives who are within the third degree and who belong to the line from which said property came.
Aims to address issues regarding Reserva Troncal as follows: it entails and encumbers property; it prevents the free circulation of property; it clusters the successional system of legitimes and of intestate succession; it penalizes marriage and legitimate family relations.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11060

rows.author: C100;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PUBLICATION OF LAWS IN THE PRINT OR ONLINE VERSION OF THE OFFICIAL GAZETTE AND OF A NEWSPAPER OF GENERAL CIRCULATION
rows.abstract:
Amends Art.2 of R.A. No.386 (Civil Code of the Phils.) to be read as follows:
Art. 2. Laws shall take effect fifteen (15) days AFTER their publication IN FULL, in the PRINT OR ONLINE VERSION OF THE Official Gazette, AND in the PRINT OR ONLINE VERSION OF A newspaper of general circulation in the Philippines, unless A DIFFERENT PERIOD is otherwise PRESCRIBED TO RESPOND TO A NATIONAL EMERGENCY:  PROVIDED, ”¦
Refers the term “LAWS” to all statutes enacted by Congress; all orders, proclamations, circulars, and other issuances promulgated by the President . . .; all rules and regulations promulgated to implement or enforce statutes pursuant to a valid delegation of legislative power”¦
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2022-07-26
